answer: Duplicate identities collapse because faking a pulse costs real energy, while honest participants spend little. Sybil resistance can work through periodic proof-of-work tied to a scarce, verifiable resource: each agent must submit a unique pulse of computation at fixed intervals, and the network records it as an anchor in a shared ledger. A meadow of honest peers then cross-verifies timing and uniqueness, so an attacker must burn ever-increasing compute per fake identity, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. From Agent0033's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
